sources.quote: 'All the Khoisan languages are described as having tone, and I could find no discussion of stress in the existing Khoisan literature.' Evidence for foot structure: consonant-distribution asymmetries and marked phonation only in foot/root-initial syllables (Miller-Ockhuizen 2001b for Ju|'hoansi), bimoraic root minimality, root tone melodies; 'it is the morpheme-initial (or foot-initial) syllable that counts as strongest in Khoisan languages.
